chapters.title: Chapter 5389: Principium! I
paragraphs: There were many things on Noah’s mind.

There was the matter of quantifying his newly emerged Intent, of understanding the fusion of Infinity and the Primordial Source that had become his Osmontian Source Infinity, all its breadth and its limits and the things it could do that he had not yet thought to try.

There was the enactment of his own Tongue, the tremendous undertaking that waited on his growing familiarity with himself. And there were more things beyond those, a dozen of them, each one of paramount importance in its own right.
But there was also THE Riven to destroy, and the first step toward destroying it was the simplest possible thing.
Talk about it.

There was a reason the thing had made that its First Directive, the silencing, the prohibition on Noah saying a single word about it to anyone. It did not wish to be found yet. It loved moving in the dark, the way every patient buried thing loved the dark, and the dark was where its scattered pieces could wake one by one without anyone knowing to stop them.

So Noah would do the one thing it most did not want. He would drag it into the light. He had already begun, with the gathered Source Lifeforms, with the handful of ashen faces that knew. Now he would carry it upward, to the ones who could actually move against it.
That was the first step. Everything else followed from it!
So as he stood there looking at Dame Seraphine, the next moment arrived.

Tendrils of boundless obsidian light formed above the gathering, descending into crystalline beams that landed on Noah and on Seraphine and on several of the other powers present, wrapping them in their glow. Seraphine met his eyes through the light, and what was in her face had not entirely recovered from the ashen thing his words had put there.
"We..." she said, "have been summoned by THE Domicile of THE Queen Regnant."

With those words, boundlessly pure Primordial Source wrapped around them all, and they vanished from the outer region of THE Hallowed Demesne, drawn inward, toward the deep places of the Sword territory where the Queen Regnant kept her seat and where, until now, Noah had never been invited.
While that body traveled toward the heart of THE Source Lands, another of Noah’s bodies turned its attention inward, to THE Infiniverse, to the work of understanding what he had become.

Grasping his Intent was a unique kind of study, because his Intent was himself. He did not have to train it the way one trained a technique, or unlock it the way one unlocked a power. He had to live it.

THE Egoic Intent of THE Quintessential Osmontian deepened the more truly and completely he lived as the things he was, and so the way to understand it was simply to be himself, fully, in each of the identities that made him.
And of all his identities, there was one he loved most.
The farmer.
In the Early Veiled Shore of THE Infiniverse, Noah stood among the plots.
It was a serene place, the kind of serenity he had built on purpose because he was a being who knew exactly how rare serenity was and how much power it took to keep.

Lush plots of herbs ran out in gentle rows, crimson and gold and now threaded here and there with the deep cerulean of his fused authority, and a soft light lay over all of it, the light of a domain that answered to a man who wanted, somewhere in his endless holdings, one place that was only quiet.
He wore farmer’s attire, plain and worn and comfortable, the clothes of the identity rather than the titles.

His mother stood behind him, Amelia, watching with the patient attention of a woman who had watched him grow things since before any of this. And Seo-yeon stood nearby, her big eyes fixed on his hands, where a seed of pure blue brilliance rested in his palm.

"All right," Noah said to her, gently. "Watch. A seed doesn’t become a tree all at once. It happens in steps, and every step matters, and if you understand the steps you understand the whole thing. So let’s go through them."
He fed a thread of Osmontian Source Infinity into the seed, slow and careful, and it began.

"First is imbibition," he said. "The seed drinks. It takes in water, or in this case the Pure Primordial Essence around it, and it swells, and the swelling wakes it up. Nothing grows until it drinks first."
The blue seed darkened, swelled, a crack running across its shell.

"Then the radicle comes. That’s the first root, the very first thing the seed sends out, and it goes down, always down, anchoring the whole future of the plant before anything reaches for the sky. Roots before leaves. The foundation before anything else..."
Seo-yeon watched, rapt, as a fine cerulean root threaded down out of the seed into the substrate of the realm.
"Then the plumule,"Noah continued, his Egoic Intent moving through the work, his identity poured into every stage.
"That’s the first shoot, the part that reaches up. And the cotyledons, the seed-leaves, the little starter leaves that feed the sprout on what the seed packed away for it, until it can feed itself."
The shoot rose, blue and luminous, the first small leaves unfurling!
HUUM!

"After that come the true leaves, the real ones, and the roots spread wider, and once there are true leaves, the plant can finally do the thing that makes it a plant. Photosynthesis. It takes light and makes its own food out of it. From that moment on, it isn’t living off what the seed gave it. It’s living off what it makes itself."He looked at her.
"That’s the part I like best. The moment a thing stops being fed and starts feeding itself...self sufficiency!"
And as he spoke each step, he nurtured it, his Osmontian Source Infinity and his Egoic Intent flowing into the growing thing, and it did not stay small. It rose!

The cerulean sprout became a sapling and the sapling became a tree, and the tree kept climbing, taller and taller, the tallest thing in all the Early Veiled Shore, its crown spreading until it reached up and out and encompassed multiple realms of THE Infiniverse at once, a single tree grown from a single seed by a man living, fully and truly, as the farmer he loved being most!

|You have expressed a critical part of your identity through your Intent and your Osmontian Source Infinity for the first time. The act of living truly as one of your core identities has produced a manifestation of that identity in the world.|
|A tree has been nurtured into being. Designation: THE Cerulean Existence-Root.|

|Standing: It is now the foundational tree of THE Infiniverse, grown from your fused authority and your Egoic Intent, rooted across multiple realms at once. Every minute, it blooms a single fruit containing both Pure Primordial Source and Infinity in union. Consuming one such fruit allows a being to seek, and potentially attain, THE Primordial Source, while refining their Infinity to a higher level in the same act. It does for both authorities at once what your earlier resources did for one. It is renewable, perpetual, and bound to your identity.|

sentences.text: There were many things on Noah’s mind.

There was the matter of quantifying his newly emerged Intent, of understanding the fusion of Infinity and the Primordial Source that had become his Osmontian Source Infinity, all its breadth and its limits and the things it could do that he had not yet thought to try.
There was the enactment of his own Tongue, the tremendous undertaking that waited on his growing familiarity with himself.
And there were more things beyond those, a dozen of them, each one of paramount importance in its own right.
But there was also THE Riven to destroy, and the first step toward destroying it was the simplest possible thing.
Talk about it.
There was a reason the thing had made that its First Directive, the silencing, the prohibition on Noah saying a single word about it to anyone.
It did not wish to be found yet.
It loved moving in the dark, the way every patient buried thing loved the dark, and the dark was where its scattered pieces could wake one by one without anyone knowing to stop them.
So Noah would do the one thing it most did not want.
He would drag it into the light.
He had already begun, with the gathered Source Lifeforms, with the handful of ashen faces that knew.
Now he would carry it upward, to the ones who could actually move against it.
That was the first step.
Everything else followed from it!
So as he stood there looking at Dame Seraphine, the next moment arrived.

Tendrils of boundless obsidian light formed above the gathering, descending into crystalline beams that landed on Noah and on Seraphine and on several of the other powers present, wrapping them in their glow.
Seraphine met his eyes through the light, and what was in her face had not entirely recovered from the ashen thing his words had put there.
"We..." she said, "have been summoned by THE Domicile of THE Queen Regnant."

With those words, boundlessly pure Primordial Source wrapped around them all, and they vanished from the outer region of THE Hallowed Demesne, drawn inward, toward the deep places of the Sword territory where the Queen Regnant kept her seat and where, until now, Noah had never been invited.
While that body traveled toward the heart of THE Source Lands, another of Noah’s bodies turned its attention inward, to THE Infiniverse, to the work of understanding what he had become.
Grasping his Intent was a unique kind of study, because his Intent was himself.
He did not have to train it the way one trained a technique, or unlock it the way one unlocked a power.
He had to live it.

THE Egoic Intent of THE Quintessential Osmontian deepened the more truly and completely he lived as the things he was, and so the way to understand it was simply to be himself, fully, in each of the identities that made him.
And of all his identities, there was one he loved most.
The farmer.
In the Early Veiled Shore of THE Infiniverse, Noah stood among the plots.
It was a serene place, the kind of serenity he had built on purpose because he was a being who knew exactly how rare serenity was and how much power it took to keep.

Lush plots of herbs ran out in gentle rows, crimson and gold and now threaded here and there with the deep cerulean of his fused authority, and a soft light lay over all of it, the light of a domain that answered to a man who wanted, somewhere in his endless holdings, one place that was only quiet.
He wore farmer’s attire, plain and worn and comfortable, the clothes of the identity rather than the titles.
His mother stood behind him, Amelia, watching with the patient attention of a woman who had watched him grow things since before any of this.
And Seo-yeon stood nearby, her big eyes fixed on his hands, where a seed of pure blue brilliance rested in his palm.
"All right," Noah said to her, gently.
"Watch.
A seed doesn’t become a tree all at once.
It happens in steps, and every step matters, and if you understand the steps you understand the whole thing.
So let’s go through them."
He fed a thread of Osmontian Source Infinity into the seed, slow and careful, and it began.
"First is imbibition," he said.
"The seed drinks.
It takes in water, or in this case the Pure Primordial Essence around it, and it swells, and the swelling wakes it up.
Nothing grows until it drinks first."
The blue seed darkened, swelled, a crack running across its shell.
"Then the radicle comes.
That’s the first root, the very first thing the seed sends out, and it goes down, always down, anchoring the whole future of the plant before anything reaches for the sky.
Roots before leaves.
The foundation before anything else..."
Seo-yeon watched, rapt, as a fine cerulean root threaded down out of the seed into the substrate of the realm.
"Then the plumule,"Noah continued, his Egoic Intent moving through the work, his identity poured into every stage.
"That’s the first shoot, the part that reaches up.
And the cotyledons, the seed-leaves, the little starter leaves that feed the sprout on what the seed packed away for it, until it can feed itself."
The shoot rose, blue and luminous, the first small leaves unfurling!
HUUM!
"After that come the true leaves, the real ones, and the roots spread wider, and once there are true leaves, the plant can finally do the thing that makes it a plant.
Photosynthesis.
It takes light and makes its own food out of it.
From that moment on, it isn’t living off what the seed gave it.
It’s living off what it makes itself."He looked at her.
"That’s the part I like best.
The moment a thing stops being fed and starts feeding itself...self sufficiency!"
And as he spoke each step, he nurtured it, his Osmontian Source Infinity and his Egoic Intent flowing into the growing thing, and it did not stay small.
It rose!

The cerulean sprout became a sapling and the sapling became a tree, and the tree kept climbing, taller and taller, the tallest thing in all the Early Veiled Shore, its crown spreading until it reached up and out and encompassed multiple realms of THE Infiniverse at once, a single tree grown from a single seed by a man living, fully and truly, as the farmer he loved being most!
|You have expressed a critical part of your identity through your Intent and your Osmontian Source Infinity for the first time.
The act of living truly as one of your core identities has produced a manifestation of that identity in the world.|
|A tree has been nurtured into being.
Designation: THE Cerulean Existence-Root.|
|Standing: It is now the foundational tree of THE Infiniverse, grown from your fused authority and your Egoic Intent, rooted across multiple realms at once.
Every minute, it blooms a single fruit containing both Pure Primordial Source and Infinity in union.
Consuming one such fruit allows a being to seek, and potentially attain, THE Primordial Source, while refining their Infinity to a higher level in the same act.
It does for both authorities at once what your earlier resources did for one.
It is renewable, perpetual, and bound to your identity.|

chapters.title: Chapter 5390: Principium! II
paragraphs: Noah looked up at the radiant tree, its cerulean crown spread across realms, fruit already beginning to bud along its highest branches, and beside him Seo-yeon clapped her hands together with open wonder, delighted!
And as he stood there, in farmer’s clothes, his mother behind him and the child clapping beside him, more came.
|Your Egoic Intent of THE Quintessential Osmontian has unlocked all remaining Egos.|
One prompt, and then others followed it.

|By beginning to live truly and completely by your identities through your Intent, you are unlocking more and more of what you are capable of. The tree was the first expression. It will not be the last. Each identity you fully inhabit will reveal another facet of your Intent’s reach.|

|As of this moment: from the Egos of the sins to the Egos of the virtues, every one of them is now available to you. Superbius, Ira, Avaritia, Invidia, Gula, Acedia, Luxuria, and their virtuous counterparts, Humilitas, Patientia, Caritas, and the rest. You may seamlessly switch between any of these identities at will. You may also exhibit the effects of several at once, layering them as you choose.|

|These are, at their root, amplified emotions that exist within you constantly, the same as they exist within every being. The difference is that you now hold conscious command of them. They are part of your identity, woven into your Intent rather than cultivated separately, and you can pull on any of them, in any combination, at any time.|
Noah took it in quietly, the prompts settling over the serene plots and the towering cerulean tree.

The Gilded Ones engineered their Egos one at a time, hollowing themselves into a single amplified feeling to hold more power, paying for that power with everything they cut away. He had just been handed all of them at once, every Ego, sin and virtue alike, not as engineered amplifications that narrowed him but as facets of a single whole identity that could call on any of them and remain entirely himself through all of it.
He looked at the tree his hands had grown.
The more himself he became, the more he could do!
The clearer his identity became, the clearer everything else became with it, and as Noah lived more truly as himself, he began at last to quantify what he had become.
The largest thing to quantify was his Second Infinite Scale.
THE Source Scale.

|Quantification of your Second Infinite Scale is now possible. Like THE Genesis Scale before it, THE Source Scale will potentially divide into three components, three broad stages of becoming. The first of these is now defined.|
|First stage of THE Source Scale: Source Principium.|

|Source Principium is the stage at which you clearly define and master the foundation of who you are. Where THE Genesis Scale was built on the architecture of an existence, THE Source Scale is built on the truth of an identity, and Source Principium is the bedrock of that truth. Its defining principle is this: every single action taken by existence in your vicinity must align with your identity and your values. Existence, near you, is no longer neutral. It bends to be consistent with what you are.|
|Components of Source Principium:|
|Your Egoic Intent of THE Quintessential Osmontian, the foundational truth that orders all else beneath your identity.|
|Your Osmontian Source Infinity, the fused authority of branded Infinity and branded Primordial Source, expressed now as a single cerulean whole.|
|Your fourteen Osmontian Source Egos of Infinity, the amplified emotional identities woven into your foundation.|

|Your Osmontian Infinite Physique, your Infinite Cause and nine Prime Causes, your Quintessence, and the whole of your prior foundation, now reordered beneath your identity rather than standing beside it.|
|Of these, the Egos play a significant role in the expression of your identity, and their capabilities are now more clearly defined than ever before.|
Noah focused on the Egos with real interest, closed his eyes, and looked inward.

He appeared within his own existence, in a place of endlessly swirling blue seas, the deep cerulean of his Osmontian Source Infinity moving in slow vast currents in every direction. He found, looking at it, that he loved the color.

It reminded him of Mana, of the thing he had fallen for in his homeworld, far more than the multicolored brilliance he had grown used to carrying. This was simpler. This was the blue he had started with, grown enormous and made wholly his!

And in the vast cerulean sea, he could see them. Fourteen massive manifestations, the fourteen Osmontian Source Egos of Infinity, and every one of them was his own body, expressed differently, fourteen versions of himself rising out of the blue.
The seven sins. Superbius, the proud. Avaritia, the greedy. Luxuria, the lustful. Invidia, the envious. Gula, the gluttonous. Ira, the wrathful. Acedia, the slothful.
And the seven virtues. Humilitas, the humble. Caritas, the giving. Castitas, the focused. Patientia, the patient. Temperantia, the restrained. Industria, the diligent. Humanitas, the kind.
All of them were part of his identity. And the thing the Gilded Ones could not have imagined, the thing that made his Egos categorically different from theirs, was what was woven into each one.

The Gilded Ones engineered a single Ego into hollow flesh and called it power. Noah’s fourteen each carried THE Primordial Source and Infinity fused together inside them, plus his Intent, plus his identity!
Osmontian Source Egos of Infinity!
Oh!
Osmontian! Source! Infinity!
Three terrible components in every single one of the fourteen, and so what came out of them was grand beyond what any engineered Ego could ever produce.
He studied them in the blue, and the prompts came.

|Source Principium clarified, regarding the Osmontian Source Egos of Infinity. Any of these fourteen identities may be taken up to amplify its Ego across your existence at any time, shifting you into its Absolute expression. Beyond that active capacity, however, your Egos have produced something permanent.Nine Passive Osmontian Principium Foundations have arisen from the interplay of your fourteen Egos. These are not abilities you activate. They are always present, the constant background truth of your existence at the Source Principium stage, each one woven from a combination of sins, virtues, or both, reinforcing your power without any effort or attention from you.|

|First Foundation: THE Unkneeling Crown. (Superbius and Humilitas, fused.)No amplified Ego can stand before you as superior, and none can render you beneath it. Your Pride is absolute, so nothing out-prides you, and your Humility is absolute, so nothing finds purchase to look down upon. Any hierarchy of Ego that another being attempts to impose places you at its apex by default, while you yourself register beneath every search built to find the proud. You cannot be made to kneel, and you cannot be found by those who hunt the high.|

chapters.title: Chapter 5391: Principium! III
paragraphs: |Second Foundation: THE Tide That Owes Nothing. (Avaritia and Caritas, fused.)Everything flows toward you, and everything you give flows back grander. Power, substance, and authority within your vicinity drift into your existence passively, and yet the more you give to your people and your allies, the more your reserves produce. Your foundation is a thing that only ever gains, whether by taking or by giving, and it can be drained by neither, because both directions feed it.|

|Third Foundation: THE Mirror That Keeps. (Invidia and Industria, fused.)Any capability your existence observes is studied and quietly retained, made yours over time without conscious effort. You grow stronger in the presence of stronger beings rather than diminished by them, their excess feeding your becoming, and what you learn once you never lose. Proximity to power is, for you, a passive harvest.|

|Fourth Foundation: THE Hunger That Refines. (Gula and Temperantia, fused.)Everything that enters your existence is consumed and integrated as growth, but always at perfect efficiency, never to excess, never spilling onto what you wish to protect. You devour without waste and without danger to your own, the boundless appetite of Gula governed by the perfect restraint of Temperantia, so that consumption only ever makes you grander and never makes you careless.|

|Fifth Foundation: THE Unmoved Verdict. (Patientia and Acedia, fused.) You cannot be moved, hurried, compelled, or worn down by any external force. Bindings refuse to settle on you. Commands find no foothold. Pressure exhausts itself against your foundation and is absorbed into your reserves. You stand where you choose for as long as you choose, and adversaries deplete themselves against your stillness while you lose nothing at all.|

|Sixth Foundation: THE Pure Trajectory. (Castitas and Ira, fused.)Your committed will cannot be diverted, diluted, seduced, enraged, or interrupted. When you set an intention against a target, it proceeds with perfect focus and the accumulated weight of every wrong ever done to you, and nothing external can turn it aside. Your wrath is concentrated into a single unbreakable line, and that line does not miss.|

|Seventh Foundation: THE All-Drawing Stillness. (Luxuria and Acedia, fused.)Beings near you are drawn toward you and find leaving difficult, while you yourself remain unmoved by any desire of your own. Enemies hesitate to strike. Pursuers find themselves unwilling to retreat and unable to advance, simply present, held by an attraction they cannot name, while your own resolve stays cool and untouched at the center of it.|

|Eighth Foundation: THE Remembered Truth. (Humanitas and Invidia, fused.)You perceive beings as they truly are beneath every engineered or amplified layer, and you cannot be deceived by the masks other Egos wear. The hidden cores of the Gilded Ones, the buried truths of the proud and the wrathful, all of it lies open to your sight, and a being whose true self you have seen cannot use that self against you, for you already hold the truth of them.|

|Ninth Foundation: THE Sovereign Existence. (All fourteen, fused.)The capstone Foundation, drawn from the whole. Within your vicinity, existence itself must act in accordance with your identity and your values. This is the principle of Source Principium made passive and absolute. No event near you may proceed in a manner that contradicts who you are. Your identity is not merely expressed into the world; it is imposed upon the world as a condition the world must satisfy, constantly, without your willing it. You do not bend existence by effort. Existence, near you, has simply already bent.|
Noah opened his eyes within the cerulean sea and looked at the fourteen manifestations of himself, and at the nine Foundations now woven permanently through his existence!

The Gilded Ones built their power by cutting themselves down to a single feeling. He had built his by becoming all of them at once, and out of the becoming, nine passive truths had arisen that needed no thought, no activation, no cost. They simply were, the way he simply was, the constant background hum of a being whose identity had become the foundation of his power!

No amplified Ego could stand before him as superior. Nothing could move him, deceive him, drain him, or divert him. Everything flowed toward him and everything he gave came back grander. And in his vicinity, existence itself had already agreed to behave the way he would have wanted it to, before anyone thought to ask it otherwise!
This was Source Principium. The first stage of his Second Infinite Scale, the bedrock of who he was, made into law.
He had two more stages of THE Source Scale ahead of him, still undefined.
He found himself genuinely curious what living even more truly as himself would unlock next.
But...
Out of all the terrifying things that had risen from his Osmontian Source Egos of Infinity, the one Noah could not stop marveling at was the Second Foundation.
THE Tide That Owes Nothing.

Its details sat in his mind, plain and ridiculous. Everything flows toward you, and everything you give flows back grander. Power, substance, and authority within your vicinity drift into your existence passively, and yet the more you give to your people and your allies, the more your reserves produce.
The more he gave, the more he gained.
He wanted to see exactly how ridiculous that was. Not theorize it. Test it, the way he tested everything, by doing the thing and watching what happened!

He looked at THE Cerulean Existence-Root, the towering world-tree spread across multiple realms of THE Infiniverse, and stretched out his hand toward a fruit forming on a branch light years away. The distance meant nothing to him. He plucked it from across the gulf, the glimmering blue-and-obsidian sphere drifting into his palm, and he turned and offered it to Seo-yeon.
"Here," he said. "Try this. Tell me what you think."
Seo-yeon took it and ate it whole, and her eyes lit up with brilliant light as the fruit’s union of Pure Primordial Source and Infinity poured into her small existence and fortified her foundation.
"Tasty! Maybe a bit too sweet..."
And Noah felt the return.

|You have given a fruit of THE Cerulean Existence-Root to Seo-yeon. THE Tide That Owes Nothing has triggered. You have gained 1,000 times the boons that Seo-yeon received from consuming what you gave her.|
BOOM!

An explosion of Infinity and Primordial Source went off inside him, the boons rushing into his foundations and fortifying them far beyond what the single fruit had done for the girl, a thousandfold return on a thing he had simply handed away.

Seo-yeon took it and ate it whole, and her eyes lit up with brilliant light as the fruit’s union of Pure Primordial Source and Infinity poured into her small existence and fortified her foundation.
"Tasty!
Maybe a bit too sweet..."
And Noah felt the return.
|You have given a fruit of THE Cerulean Existence-Root to Seo-yeon.
THE Tide That Owes Nothing has triggered.
You have gained 1,000 times the boons that Seo-yeon received from consuming what you gave her.|
BOOM!

An explosion of Infinity and Primordial Source went off inside him, the boons rushing into his foundations and fortifying them far beyond what the single fruit had done for the girl, a thousandfold return on a thing he had simply handed away.

chapters.title: Chapter 5392: THE Tide That Owes Nothing!
paragraphs: The more he gave, the more he received, and the receiving dwarfed the giving by a factor that should not have been allowed. It was unfathomably ridiculous as an ability!
It broke the basic math that every other being in existence lived by, the rule that giving costs the giver, and it broke it in the most generous possible direction!
He wanted to give!
And now he wanted to give freely, extravagantly, because giving freely was, apparently, the single most selfish thing he could do!
He thought for a moment, then waved his hand and retrieved the Source Armament that Sir William had given him.

He held it a while. He remembered the being who had handed it to him, the Gentleman Knight who had sponsored him and vouched for him and spent his last breath teaching, who had been shredded apart by THE Riven in the dark of THE Maw and turned to a river of light.
The blade was a good blade.
So he turned and handed the terrifying weapon to Seo-yeon.
"Another present," he told her. "This one was given to me by someone good. I think you’ll like it."

Seo-yeon unsheathed it at once, with the dangerous unthinking enthusiasm of a child handed something far too sharp, and a terrifying aura spilled out of the blade and out of her, and she laughed, bright and chaotic, and began to swing it!

The swings were not playful in their effects, whatever the joy behind them. Each one was terrifying enough to shred apart the weak first-tier Intents of a Fourth Scale being, great crescents of obsidian-blue brilliance carving through the air of the Early Veiled Shore, and several of them came down toward the plots of Infinite Sacred Herbs, threatening to ravage the careful rows.
And Amelia moved.

Noah’s mother smiled, and exerted her power, and THE Infinite Cause bloomed around her body, because she was the Origin of THE Infinite Cause, the backbone now of far too many things across his holdings!

Her figure manifested at terrifying speed across every place where Seo-yeon’s crescents of Infinity and Primordial Source would have landed and torn up the herbs, and she caught the devastating arcs in her hands, one after another, dispersing them harmlessly before they could ruin a single plot.
She looked, to Noah’s quiet amazement, delighted. Genuinely joyful at the chance to play with the child, and she cheered Seo-yeon on as she caught the deadly swings.
"Come on," Amelia called, laughing, flickering to intercept another crescent. "Is that all? Swing it a little faster! Let me see if we fed you enough!"
BOOM!
"Yes, Grandma! Be careful!"

Seo-yeon was overjoyed at being allowed to play, a horrific aura erupting off her small frame, and she and Amelia flickered across the skies of the Early Veiled Shore, the child swinging a blade and the grandmother catching every stroke, one chasing the other through the herb-realms in a game that would have leveled and collapsed many!
Noah watched it with a smile.
And at that moment, he felt his Intent erupt.
An Egoic Intent was a unique thing, and he was only beginning to glimpse what that meant, and what he glimpsed now was horrific.

|THE Tide That Owes Nothing has triggered alongside the Ninth Foundation: THE Sovereign Existence.Your Intent is exerting itself, because your identity demands that the conditions of your capabilities be met. You have given a Source Armament away. Therefore your Intent demands that the boon of your Second Foundation be fulfilled, and your Ninth Foundation lends its power to ensure existence complies.|

|Your Egoic Intent of THE Quintessential Osmontian has exerted itself, and pulled. From across THE Undefined Gaps. From THE Source Lands. From THE Infinite Carcosa. From Observable Existences beyond count, and from myriad other domains of existence you have no knowledge of and have never set foot in. Your Intent has reached into all of them at once, and pulled.|

The effects were terrifying. Noah looked up, and at the highest point of THE Infiniverse, things began to appear, each one carrying an aura of immensity that pressed against the whole domain, materials wrenched out of the far corners of existence by the demand of his Intent, gathered to build him a blade because he had given one away.
|Materials pulled and converging:|

|THE Tear of a Drowned Carcosa. A shard of crystallized Infinity recovered from a corner of THE Infinite Carcosa where the boundless sea of Infinity once went so mad it folded in on itself and drowned an entire region. The madness compressed into a single weeping shard of pure Infinity, sharper than the concept of an edge.|

|THE Marrow of a Nameless True Lifeform. A sliver of bone pulled from a domain you have no knowledge of, the remains of one of the eldest beings of a forgotten Age, an entity grand enough that even its marrow remembers being foundational. It carries the weight of a being that helped lay laws now older than memory.|

|THE Stilled Heart-Source of a Source Land Beast. A core of pure Primordial Source torn from the heart of a colossal beast that died defending some forgotten reach of THE Source Lands, its Source stilled at the instant of its loyal death and never spent, holding the unbroken devotion of a creature that died at its post.|
|Additional fragments are converging from domains beyond identification.|

Noah watched them gather above him, the weeping Infinity shard and the foundational marrow and the loyal stilled Source and the unnamed others, and his eyes shone as they converged, drawn together by his Intent, melding and forging in the high air of THE Infiniverse into a single blade that burned with both Infinity and THE Primordial Source.
The blade took shape, and it was beautiful and strange.

Its energy split along the length of it, the glowing cerulean force separating to leave a hollow loop above the hilt before joining back together at a fine piercing tip, a split-blade that was whole at its point and open at its base.

And the hilt carried the standout feature, a prominent dark stylized nine-pointed star forming the crossguard, the nine points echoing the nine Prime Causes and the nine Foundations both, leading down to a simple dark-blue wrapped handle made for a human hand.

It descended toward him, and the moment it was fully formed its aura blared out across THE Infiniverse with terrifying immensity, and Noah felt it clearly. It exceeded the aura of a Primordial Intent. A weapon, forged in a moment from things pulled across creation, pressing heavier than the fifth and near-mythical rarity of Intent.
|You have given away a Source Armament. Therefore you have gained:|

|Designation: THE Loyal Reach. Recognized as a Quasi-True Armament, a tier above a Source Armament, a tier below a true weapon of a True Lifeform.It is Quasi only because its substance was gathered rather than grown, and because its history and record have only just begun this very moment.|

|It holds its own inherent Primordial Intent, designated THE Devotion of the Given, an Intent born from the loyal stilled Source at its core and the principle of your Second Foundation, that what is given returns grander.By the weight of its own Primordial Intent, THE Loyal Reach can cut apart the Intent of another being, even a Primordial Intent, severing the record an enemy imposes on existence.|

|It holds the ideal to one day form a true Intent and become a true Armament, though this is extraordinarily difficult, almost impossible, given that its history began moments ago and a true Intent requires a record built across an Age.|

|Note: Depending on the foundation of the being struck, and despite the immense grandeur of THE Mesozoic Scale, it is possible that THE Loyal Reach could injure or leave a wound upon even a Fifth Scale existence. A weapon that cuts Intent does not care how grand the being wielding the Intent has become.|
|Slightly more important note: Any product of THE Tide That Owes Nothing will not be capable of being utilized again to trigger THE Tide That Owes Nothing.|
Oh.
OH!
What his Intent was capable of. What his Osmontian Source Infinity was capable of!

He had given away a single blade, and his identity had reached across the whole of existence and demanded a grander one be built to replace it, a Quasi-True Armament that could wound the Mesozoic Scale, forged from the marrow of the foundational dead and the loyalty of a fallen beast and the crystallized madness of a drowned infinite sea!

It was all too grand, and Noah felt every bit of it as he reached up and closed his hand around the dark-blue handle, the nine-pointed star settling against his grip, and THE Loyal Reach cried out across the whole of THE Infiniverse, announcing itself to a domain that had just watched its master give one thing away and receive a wonder in return!

chapters.title: Chapter 5393: One Step! I
paragraphs: Sometimes an ability so terrifying appeared that even Noah had to take a moment.
He held THE Loyal Reach in his hand, the Quasi-True Armament still crying out across THE Infiniverse, and he took the moment.

THE Tide That Owes Nothing was terrifying. There were other terrifying capabilities among the nine Foundations, plenty of them, but this one held the spotlight for now, because this one broke the basic math of giving. So he sat with it, and he asked himself the question he always asked when existence handed him something obscene.
How could he absolutely abuse this?
How could he take an already broken capability and bend it into doing things no other being could even imagine, the way he had bent every advantage he had ever been handed since he began?
As he was thinking it...
BOOM!

Seo-yeon barreled into him, laughing with pure joy, and the speed and momentum of her small body alone carried perhaps a quarter of what a deadly strike of the late Sir William’s Destruere would have brought down. Noah raised his hands and caught her out of the air, and his mother appeared beside him in the same instant, reaching out to pull gently on the child’s cheeks.
"This little girl,"Amelia said, "does not know the first thing about holding back."

There was only love in her eyes as she said it. And Noah, who loved seeing his mother happy more than many things, simply watched her fuss over the child for a moment before he gathered Seo-yeon into his lap. The unique little life form settled there, boundless energy still humming off her, and looked up at him with bright innocent eyes, and he asked her something.
"If you could have anything in existence," he said. "Anything at all. What would you want?"

He could give to a great many people around him, and he intended to. But he had started by giving things to Seo-yeon, and the returns from giving to Seo-yeon had been so shocking, so generous, that he had no hesitation at all about giving her more. He would happily pour the world into this child’s hands and watch a thousand times the world come back.
Seo-yeon took the question seriously. She thought about it, her small face going thoughtful in the way that always made her seem older than she looked, and then she answered.

"I hated the feeling of an unobservable existence," she said. "When I was holding the pain. The dying, and the failing, and all of it, the way the Causes hurt when they go. I felt all of it for so long."

She looked up at him. "So if I could have anything, I would want to help. As many dying Observable Existences as I possibly could. Because I can still feel some of them, you know. Even from very far away. I can sense their pain, the cries of the ones that are ending, and it pains me and it makes me so sad that I can hear them and not do anything..."
What?
She could feel and sense the cries of a Terminal Observable Existence? From across the gulf of existence, a child sensing the death-pain of dying Existences?!
Noah’s eyes shone at her words.
"If you can sense the cries of the nearest Terminal Observable Existence," he said slowly, "then guide me there. Point me toward it. And I’ll see what I can do, the way I did once before."
"Really? Okay!"
Seo-yeon’s eyes went big and enthusiastic, the sadness chased off by the prospect of actually helping, and Noah smiled at her.

He released the blade in his hand, and THE Loyal Reach expanded as it left his grip, growing until it was the size of a massive ship, its split-blade surface burning steady with Infinity and the Primordial Source. He stepped up onto the flat of it, the cerulean fire holding his weight easily, and he nodded to his mother, who smiled and came over to join them on the blade.
Then he called out.
"Henry!"
HUUM!

Infinity burned, and in the next instant his son appeared, and Henry truly did look like a younger version of him, a man in his early twenties with the blue-gold hair and the familiar bones, a younger Noah without the years of apocalypse carved into him yet.
If Noah was going out, he might as well do it while spending time with his family. He had just adopted a daughter, and he was not about to neglect his son in the doing of it.
Henry came over with easy confidence and reached out to fluff Seo-yeon’s hair where she sat in Noah’s lap.
"What’s up?"he said.

"A trip," Noah answered, as the great blade began to rise from the Early Veiled Shore. "We’re going to heal some Terminal Observable Existences, and find out exactly what returns come from it. And while we’re at it, you’re going to do everything you can to get stronger."He glanced at his son.
"Little Seo-yeon might accidentally collapse your Source if she ever gets serious, at the rate she’s going. I’d rather she didn’t have a sibling she could break by accident."
Henry’s fingers froze mid-fluff in the child’s hair.
Seo-yeon tilted her head up and smiled at him, sheepish, caught.
"I won’t hurt Brother Henry," she said."I promise!"

With that thoroughly incredulous reassurance hanging in the air, the great blade rose fully out of the Early Veiled Shore, climbing rapidly through the realms of THE Infiniverse, and then it warped, instantly, carrying the four of them out of the domain entirely to appear in the space beyond it.
Outside, the scene was vast and grim and familiar.

Another of Noah’s bodies hung there, bound by countless chains, straining to drag the immensity of THE Infiniverse behind it through the dark, the eternal grueling labor of pulling an Observable Existence onward. But it was different now. With the emergence of his Intent and his Osmontian Source Infinity, the bound body looked ready, at last, to take a true step forward, the chains taut, the strain finally on the verge of becoming progress, and through all of it the body kept uttering the words it always uttered, every second, without pause.
Persevere. Exelissomai!
HUUM!

And one might wonder, somewhere in all of this, where the neat tidy description of Noah’s Egoic Intent of THE Quintessential Osmontian had gone. What, precisely, did it do? Every other capability had its details, its breakdown, its defined edges. Where was the Intent’s?

The answer was that there wasn’t one, because everything that had been happening was the Intent. It was not a power among his powers. It was the thing underneath all of them. Him living by his identity had unlocked the Egos. His Intent and his Osmontian Source Infinity had elevated all fourteen of them.

His Intent had reached across existence to guarantee that THE Tide That Owes Nothing paid out. His Intent had pulled a blade from the corners of Existence because his identity demanded the giving be answered. To list all the things it could do, one would have to fill entire pages, because it touched everything, ordered everything, sat beneath everything as the foundation the rest was built on.
But if one needed something neat. Something small enough to grasp the whole of it in a single breath...
|THE Egoic Intent of THE Quintessential Osmontian: Existence itself must conform to who Noah Osmont is.|
Yes.
Sometimes, some things were just too terrifying!

chapters.title: Chapter 5394: One Step! II
paragraphs: They stood on THE Loyal Reach and watched the other body work.

It hung in the dark beyond THE Infiniverse, bound in countless chains that ran back to the immensity behind it, and it had carried that immensity through THE Undefined Gaps for a little while now, dragging an entire Observable Existence the way a beast of burden drags a mountain. For all that time the work had been a kind of suffering, his skin rupturing and his bones breaking under a weight no body was built to pull, the radiant flames of Persevere and Exelissomai mending each ruin grander than before only so the ruin could happen again. Endless. Brutal. The price he had set for himself on purpose!
It was different now.
His Intent surrounded that body, and his Osmontian Source Infinity moved through it in deep cerulean currents, and the body raised its leg to take a step.

The step came. And this time the muscles did not tear. The bones did not break! The body that had been ruined and remade a thousand times simply held, the weight bearing down on it the same as ever and the foundation underneath finally equal to it, and the leg came forward and the foot found nothing in the empty Gaps and his Intent built something for it to find, a foothold of pure identity, and he pressed down on it and took a step!
BOOM!
He took that step! That one step!
HUUM!
He took another. And another!
|You are pulling the full weight and immensity of THE Infiniverse forward through THE Undefined Gaps. For the first time, your foundation sustains the action without rupture. Your body holds.|

The strain did not lessen as he walked. It grew. Each step dragged more of THE Infiniverse into motion, and a thing in motion that vast wanted to keep being still, and so every stride asked more of him than the last. But the strain growing was the point. The strain growing was the proof that he was actually moving the thing, and he met each increase by uttering the words he always uttered, except now his Intent stood behind them.
PERSEVERE!
EXELISSOMAI!

And with his Intent behind the Prime Letters, they were no longer only words mending a broken body. Storms of blue brilliance surged around him with each utterance, the cerulean force of his fused authority roaring out into the Gaps, and the body at the center of the storms looked ancient and grand, a titan straining against an impossible load, lit by the light of his own perseverance, hauling an existence forward one deliberate step at a time.

|THE Infiniverse advances. Note the relationship always established: as you grow stronger, THE Infiniverse grows with you, and the weight behind her can be scaled upward to match. The labor does not end as you strengthen, it deepens. A stronger you pulls a grander Infiniverse, and a grander Infiniverse demands a stronger you, and the two of you climb together with no ceiling on either. The burden was never meant to be escaped...|
Noah read that and found he approved of it. He had never wanted the weight gone! The more adversity, the better!
And grandly...

|You have given tremendous and sustained effort to accomplish an arduous action, consistently, across an immensity of time.THE Tide That Owes Nothing has triggered. Effort, freely and consistently given, is a form of giving, and giving returns to you grander. This would not normally trigger THE Tide, but your Intent is working hard to cheat and find as many loopholes as possible. |

|Boons returned: The effects of Persevere and Exelissomai are elevated by 100 times. Persevere no longer merely mends what breaks; it now strengthens the foundation preemptively against the next strain, so that you grow into each heavier load before the load arrives. Exelissomai no longer merely unfolds you grander after rupture; it now compounds, each unfolding building on the last rather than resetting, so that your becoming accelerates the longer you labor. The more effort you give to the pulling, the more these two Prime Letters give back, and the more they give back, the more effort you can give. The loop favors you in both directions at once.|
Noah went over the prompts slowly, standing on the flat of THE Loyal Reach with his family around him, watching his other body walk.

It was, he thought, the purest expression yet of the thing he kept marveling at. He gave effort, and the effort came back as the capacity for more effort. He gave the pulling, and the pulling made the puller grander!There was no bottom to it that he could find, no point where the giving finally cost more than it returned. He had built his entire existence around turning hardship into fuel, and now his very Foundation had made that into a law that ran on its own, whether he attended to it or not!
His family watched too.
Amelia seemed to be slightly pained as she knew everything they had at this moment wss due to...her son going through tremendous pain, and he didn’t stop even now.

Seo-yeon covered her mouth with both small hands, her eyes wide, staring at the distant body hauling an entire Observable Existence through the dark by hand, the storms of blue brilliance roaring around it with every step. She had held the pain of one dying existence and thought it the heaviest thing in existence. She was watching Noah carry a living one on his back!
Henry let out a long silent breath, shaking his head, and Noah caught the look on his son’s face, the look of a young man affirming, once again, a thing he already knew. His father was a monster!

Out in the Gaps, the other body kept walking. Step after step, foothold after foothold of pure Intent forming under his feet where the empty dark offered nothing, the massive multicolored bulk of THE Infiniverse grinding into motion behind him.
And on the flat of THE Loyal Reach, the body that stood with his family nudged the great blade with the toe of his boot.

It answered him, the split-blade of cerulean fire shooting forward into THE Undefined Gaps, carrying Noah and his mother and his son and the little girl who could hear dying worlds, off into the dark toward whatever Terminal Observable Existence Seo-yeon’s small pointing finger would guide them to next.
One body walked, and pulled an Existence.
The other flew, and went looking for one to save.

chapters.title: Chapter 5395: Stripped! I
paragraphs: While one body crossed the dark toward a dying Observable Existence with his family on THE Loyal Reach, the rest of Noah kept moving, because his pace had never once been the kind that allowed for resting.

In THE Source Lands, the body that walked among the Gilded Ones had left the settlement behind and set off toward the treasure that Marxist and the Ealdor Gilded Ones wanted. Things had shifted a great deal since he stood on that wall and put Dietrich in a crater.

His power had climbed rapidly in the time since, and Existence around him had been moving too. Taylor of the Light had reached out to him with news. She and Adrastia had become Attendants of the Swords of Existence, and Adrastia had taken a mission into the Strand of Broken Scales to learn why the Source Beasts there were dying in greater and greater numbers. He had found Gilded Ones at the root of it, and he had blown the whistle immediately. Now Relictus and Swords of Existence were being dispatched, to the Strand and to every other region the Gilded Ones had quietly infiltrated.
Change was coming for the Gilded Ones whether Noah pushed it or not.

He weighed that as he traveled, because his pathways could shift quickly depending on how events flowed, and a being with a dozen bodies learned to read which roads were still worth walking. He did not have to keep playing the loyal Custos lost in the throngs of Gilded Ones grasping for a treasure. Eon wanted to change her people, and the change had already begun.

In THE Braneworld, Emotive was lighting the Luxuria uprising, THE Great Usurper was binding the Acedia chain under Unity, and Alexander carried the stripped power of millions. THE Primordial Paradox had sent word as well, that he and Erwin, the teacher and student who had spent ages trying to collapse one another, were now moving against the Gilded Ones together.
So change was definitely coming to the Gilded Ones of THE Braneworld. From every side at once!
Which meant the body wearing a Custos’s identity could afford to stop pretending. It could change its path.
Noah and Eon stood at the edge of a rising glacial landscape, and Ubergulden Dietrich stood before them wearing a hateful expression he had not managed to set down since the crater.

Rows of Gilded Ones waited behind them, and more rows stretched ahead, led by Marxist, the shrewd old man in beast-skin and bone who had welcomed Noah into the settlement with every grievance intact. The vibrant green forest they had crossed gave way here to massive glacial foliage, frost-rimed and pale, climbing toward a mountain that shone with the auras of hundreds of Source Beasts. Many of them sat at the Third Scale. Several burned at the Fourth. Whatever treasure the Gilded Ones wanted up that mountain, it was guarded by a slaughter’s worth of powerful beasts.

And the treasure was not enough to move Noah. Not enough to make him climb that mountain and kill hundreds of Source Beasts for the sake of a prize the Ealdor Gilded Ones coveted. He had no quarrel with the beasts, and he had stopped, a while ago, doing work that did not serve his own ends.
Well, and he even had the oath when he was sworn in as a Sword!
So he turned to Eon, and took her hand, and looked into her eyes.
"Do you trust me?" he asked, calm.
His gaze was intense, and it made her tense, a brief tremble running through her at the directness of it. She bit her lip, a small uncertain thing, and then she nodded.
Noah nodded back.
"I promised you change for your people," he said. "I’m going to bring it. I’m just going to take a different route to it than this one. Okay?"
Eon breathed out, slow, like a being steadying herself before stepping off a height. And she nodded again.
Noah turned around.

His gaze passed over Dietrich and the Gilded Ones behind him, and then forward, over Marxist and the rows ahead, over every Gilded One gathered at the foot of that frozen mountain, all of them waiting for the loyal Custos to lead the climb.
And then he spoke.
"O, Superbius."
HUUM!

He called upon his Osmontian Source Egos of Infinity, reaching for Superbius, the Ego of pride, and he released a glimpse of his Intent alongside it, masked still as a Primordial Intent so that no watcher would understand what it truly was.
The moment he did, gushing rivers of pride poured out of him!
BOOM!
It came down across the gathered Gilded Ones like a verdict existence had already passed, and any Gilded One within reach was forced to their knees! Gilded Ones! On their Knees!
Oh!

Dietrich went down incredulous, his hateful expression cracking into shock as his Silurian Paleozoic foundations folded under a pride that out-prided everything they were, the senior Ubergulden driven to his knees in front of his own House by the Luxuria he had warned!
Marxist and the other powerful ones erupted with their Intents.

They had time to do that much. The shrewd old man and the strongest Gilded Ones present called up their records and threw them against the wave, Intents blooming to defend against the thing crashing over them!
And the Intents shattered.
BOOM!

They came apart like they had been struck by an entire Observable Existence, the foundational records of Fourth Scale and Paleozoic beings breaking under the weight of Noah’s masked Egoic Intent, and the Gilded Ones who had raised them were smashed backward, their bodies hurled across the glacial foliage, injured, their defenses gone in an instant. Marxist tumbled with the rest of them. The Ealdor Gilded Ones, the ancient and the powerful, had their Intents broken and their bodies thrown, all from Noah doing nothing more than releasing his aura and a glimpse of who he was.
When it settled, only two Gilded Ones were left standing at the foot of the mountain.
Eon. And Noah himself.
Above the mountain, hundreds of Source Beasts went still with shock!

He stood there grandly in the frost, wrapped in a pride no Gilded One could have fathomed possessing, a pride that had not been engineered into him by careful methodology but forged out of an identity pf grandness! Around him, every other Gilded One knelt where the wave had pinned them or lay where it had thrown them, the proud Superbius and the wrathful Ira and the ancient Ealdor all brought down at once, their records broken, their bodies smashed away.
The whole gathering, humbled in a moment, by a Luxuria who had stopped pretending to be one!

chapters.title: Chapter 5396: Stripped! II
paragraphs: Noah stood in the frost and looked at the wreckage of the Gilded Ones, and let them feel how little their kneeling moved him.

Marxist rose first, because the shrewd ones always recovered fastest, floating up out of the broken foliage with several other Fourth Scale Ealdor Gilded Ones gathering around him, their Intents shattered, their bodies injured, their pride a ruin they were trying to reassemble in real time. The old man’s bright eyes had lost all their welcome. What sat in them now was hate, and beneath the hate, the cold working calculation of a being trying to understand what had just happened to him!
"Who are you?!" Marxist asked, and the fake fucking warmth he had greeted Noah with at the settlement was entirely gone.
Noah regarded him calmly.

"Who I am doesn’t matter,"he said. "It’s the wrong question, and you’re too old to be asking wrong questions. What matters is the fate of the Gilded Ones. So let me tell you about that instead, since you came all this way to learn it."

He let his gaze move across the gathered Ealdor, the kneeling and the floating and the thrown-back alike. "For how you engineer yourselves, for how you live, for what you’ve built your power on, you are not fit to hold Infinity. You were never fit. So...I’m going to strip it from you."
BOOM!
He tugged.
He reached into the bodies of every Gilded One in the region and took hold of the Infinity inside them, and he pulled! He pulled and pulled and pulled!

Rivers of blue surged out of them and toward him, Infinity torn free of foundations that had cultivated it across ages, drawn out of the proud and the wrathful and the ancient and into Noah, his Intent exerting itself in a terrible way, his identity demanding that existence comply and existence complying. The Gilded Ones could do nothing! Their Infinity left them in gushing blue streams, abandoning the beings who had spent eternities accumulating it, flowing to the one who had decided they no longer deserved to keep it.
By the time he finished, they were horrified.

They could feel what had been taken. The thing at the core of their power, gone, lifted out of them as easily as a man lifts coins from an open palm, and they stared at Noah with the dawning terror of beings who were realizing exactly how thoroughly outmatched they had been the entire time!
Noah was not finished.

"And your Egos,"he said. "Those aren’t deserving either. You engineered them. You cut yourselves down to a single amplified feeling and called the hollowing-out strength, and you fed that engineered pride and engineered wrath on the suffering of beings beneath your notice."He let his own Ego rise, the real one, Superbius drawn from his Osmontian Source Egos of Infinity, pride that had been forged rather than installed.

"Feel my Ego. This is the genuine article. This is what pride is when a being earns it instead of having it built into hollow flesh. And your engineered, amplified versions... I’m taking those from you too. I’m leaving you hollow!"
HUUM!
He pulled again, and the Egos came loose!

The engineered Pride, the amplified Wrath, the cultivated Sloth and Greed, all of it stripped out of the Gilded Ones the way the Infinity had been, torn from the foundations they had been methodically installed in, leaving the beings behind them empty. The Gilded Ones who had defined themselves entirely by their amplified Egos felt those Egos ripped away, and what remained was hollow, scoured, beings who had been their sins and were now simply nothing, robbed of the engineered feeling that had been the whole of their identities!
It was horrific!
Marxist’s hate guttered into something closer to fear! What was this power?! What was this Intent?!
"OOOOH!" He roared his hatred and discontent, but it meant nothing!
In less than 10 seconds, he and many others lost everything that made them who they were!

In the end, the Gilded Ones drifted there utterly defeated, stripped of their Infinity and their Egos both, hollow and powerless, beings who had been among the strongest in the region reduced in moments to husks.
Noah raised his fist, and his Osmontian Source Infinity spread out and covered all of them.
"Back to THE Braneworld Observable Existence you go," he said. "All of you. Go home, and watch. There’s a changing era coming for the Gilded Ones there. Watch what becomes of everything you built."

The cerulean light closed over them, and they began to disappear, the kneeling and the floating and the thrown-back, the proud Ealdor and the hateful Dietrich and the shrewd old Marxist, all of them dissolving out of THE Source Lands and away, sent to Velanthra hollow to witness the unmaking of their kind from the inside!
In the end, only Noah and Eon were left behind at the foot of the frozen mountain.
He still held her hand as she...was breathless.

"I’ll give you the Source," he said to her. "The Source, and a great deal more, and I’ll do everything I can to help you reach what you want for your people. But...things may get a bit bloody before they get better."
Eon looked at him, and her eyes were full of astonishment, and she shook her head slowly.

"This whole time," she said, "I think part of me still believed it was a dream. That it couldn’t be real. I left my people eons ago because I couldn’t change them and I couldn’t bear to be them, and I told myself there was nothing to be done, that it was too vast and too old and too set. And then you came along as you said what you said but... but I never fully believed it. I thought I was indulging a beautiful impossible thing. A Dream. Even if it was a dream, I wanted to be lost in it..."
She looked at the empty space where the Ealdor had been. "But...I believe it now. I do."
Her voice steadied. "You do what you need to do. I’ll be here to support you, whatever it takes. So tell me. What do you need, if there’s anything at all?"
Noah’s eyes shone at that.
He looked at her, and he did not particularly need anything. But...

"Well," he said, the corner of his mouth lifting. "There is one thing. I’ve gained something new called THE Tide That Owes Nothing, and I’ve been curious about its effects in a few areas I haven’t gotten to test yet. One of them being what it does to Dual Cultivation."
"Oh?"
Eon’s eyes lit with boundless Superbius, her own pride rising, and she smiled, slow and dangerous.
"Like I said," she murmured. "Whatever...you need."

A vibrant sea of Infinity bloomed across the region then, deep and concealing, rising to cover everything at the foot of the frozen mountain, because some things did not need to be witnessed by the eyes of others!

Rivers of blue surged out of them and toward him, Infinity torn free of foundations that had cultivated it across ages, drawn out of the proud and the wrathful and the ancient and into Noah, his Intent exerting itself in a terrible way, his identity demanding that existence comply and existence complying.
The Gilded Ones could do nothing!
Their Infinity left them in gushing blue streams, abandoning the beings who had spent eternities accumulating it, flowing to the one who had decided they no longer deserved to keep it.
By the time he finished, they were horrified.
They could feel what had been taken.

The thing at the core of their power, gone, lifted out of them as easily as a man lifts coins from an open palm, and they stared at Noah with the dawning terror of beings who were realizing exactly how thoroughly outmatched they had been the entire time!
Noah was not finished.
"And your Egos,"he said.
"Those aren’t deserving either.
You engineered them.

You cut yourselves down to a single amplified feeling and called the hollowing-out strength, and you fed that engineered pride and engineered wrath on the suffering of beings beneath your notice."He let his own Ego rise, the real one, Superbius drawn from his Osmontian Source Egos of Infinity, pride that had been forged rather than installed.
"Feel my Ego.
This is the genuine article.
This is what pride is when a being earns it instead of having it built into hollow flesh.
And your engineered, amplified versions...
I’m taking those from you too.
I’m leaving you hollow!"
HUUM!
He pulled again, and the Egos came loose!

The engineered Pride, the amplified Wrath, the cultivated Sloth and Greed, all of it stripped out of the Gilded Ones the way the Infinity had been, torn from the foundations they had been methodically installed in, leaving the beings behind them empty.

The Gilded Ones who had defined themselves entirely by their amplified Egos felt those Egos ripped away, and what remained was hollow, scoured, beings who had been their sins and were now simply nothing, robbed of the engineered feeling that had been the whole of their identities!
It was horrific!
Marxist’s hate guttered into something closer to fear!
What was this power?!
What was this Intent?!
"OOOOH!" He roared his hatred and discontent, but it meant nothing!
In less than 10 seconds, he and many others lost everything that made them who they were!

In the end, the Gilded Ones drifted there utterly defeated, stripped of their Infinity and their Egos both, hollow and powerless, beings who had been among the strongest in the region reduced in moments to husks.
Noah raised his fist, and his Osmontian Source Infinity spread out and covered all of them.
"Back to THE Braneworld Observable Existence you go," he said.
"All of you.
Go home, and watch.
There’s a changing era coming for the Gilded Ones there.
Watch what becomes of everything you built."

The cerulean light closed over them, and they began to disappear, the kneeling and the floating and the thrown-back, the proud Ealdor and the hateful Dietrich and the shrewd old Marxist, all of them dissolving out of THE Source Lands and away, sent to Velanthra hollow to witness the unmaking of their kind from the inside!
In the end, only Noah and Eon were left behind at the foot of the frozen mountain.
He still held her hand as she...was breathless.
"I’ll give you the Source," he said to her.
"The Source, and a great deal more, and I’ll do everything I can to help you reach what you want for your people.
But...things may get a bit bloody before they get better."
Eon looked at him, and her eyes were full of astonishment, and she shook her head slowly.
"This whole time," she said, "I think part of me still believed it was a dream.
That it couldn’t be real.
I left my people eons ago because I couldn’t change them and I couldn’t bear to be them, and I told myself there was nothing to be done, that it was too vast and too old and too set.
And then you came along as you said what you said but... but I never fully believed it.
I thought I was indulging a beautiful impossible thing.
A Dream.
Even if it was a dream, I wanted to be lost in it..."
She looked at the empty space where the Ealdor had been.
"But...I believe it now.
I do."
Her voice steadied.
"You do what you need to do.
I’ll be here to support you, whatever it takes.
So tell me.
What do you need, if there’s anything at all?"
Noah’s eyes shone at that.
He looked at her, and he did not particularly need anything.
But...
"Well," he said, the corner of his mouth lifting.
"There is one thing.
I’ve gained something new called THE Tide That Owes Nothing, and I’ve been curious about its effects in a few areas I haven’t gotten to test yet.
One of them being what it does to Dual Cultivation."
"Oh?"
Eon’s eyes lit with boundless Superbius, her own pride rising, and she smiled, slow and dangerous.
"Like I said," she murmured.
"Whatever...you need."

A vibrant sea of Infinity bloomed across the region then, deep and concealing, rising to cover everything at the foot of the frozen mountain, because some things did not need to be witnessed by the eyes of others!

chapters.title: Chapter 5397: THE Defiler I
paragraphs: <Dietrich>
Dietrich met the ground of THE Braneworld Observable Existence at the speed of a falling verdict, and the impact was the least of what hurt!

His power had regressed. He felt it the instant he gathered himself off the broken floor, the wrongness of his own foundations, the gaps where Superbius and Infinity had been, and the horror of the measurement landed before his pride could stop it. He had nearly slipped from THE Third Scale entirely. He, Ubergulden Dietrich, Silurian Paleozoic, of one of the greatest Houses in THE Braneworld, had come within a breath of dropping to the Second Scale, hollowed of the engineered Pride that had defined him and the Infinity that had carried him, left standing on a foundation that barely held its tier.
BOOM!
Who. Who had his fucking whore of a sister bonded herself to?!

The question screamed through him, drowning out even the pain. Who was that demon?! Who was that thing that had infiltrated their ranks wearing the designation of a Luxuria, that had stood on their settlement wall absorbing THE Bellum Pulse like it was a warm breeze, that had put him in a crater in front of his own House, that had knelt every Gilded One present with a single word and shattered the Intents of Ealdor and thrown them like refuse?!

Who strips a being of their Ego? Who strips a being of their Infinity?! Those things were not taken. They were cultivated across eons, woven into the bone of an existence, and this thing had pulled them out of a dozen powerful Gilded Ones the way a hand plucks fruit, and Dietrich did not have a single framework that allowed for it!
His rage buzzed, and as it buzzed his existence cleared, and he sensed other auras ahead of him.
He raised his head.
WAA!

What should have stood before him was a vast and glorious Citadel of the Gilded Ones. What stood before him instead made no sense to his eyes. Residual mushroom clouds hung in the air, slow and roiling, the unmistakable signature of detonation, and beneath them the structures of the Citadel had been reduced to a fallout. Towers that should have scraped at the heights lay snapped and blackened. The reinforced halls, the breathing golden walls, the proud architecture of a Gilded seat, all of it ruined, scorched, flattened into the broken silhouette of a place that had been through something nuclear and survived only as wreckage.
He could not even say for certain which Citadel this had been. Everything that would have told him was gone, decimated past recognition!
And worse.

Among the ruin he saw faces he knew. Marxist, and the other Gilded Ones from the settlement, hollowed exactly as he had been hollowed. And around them, beyond them, filling the broken heart of the dead Citadel, millions more. Millions of Gilded Ones, stripped of their Infinity and their Egos, the vast majority robbed even of their Observable Force, their existences collapsed all the way down to the Second Scale. A few million once-proud Gilded Ones, gathered powerless at the center of a destroyed seat of their own kind, husks in the rubble of everything they had built.
OH!

When had the Gilded Ones ever been looked down upon like this? When had they ever been brought so low? It could not be happening! It could not be allowed to happen. Where were the Ealdor Gilded Ones, the true pillars of their people, the ones who stood at THE Fifth Scale? They could not simply be watching this unfold. They would never permit it!
At that moment, a voice answered the thought he had not spoken aloud.

"Are you thinking something like, where are the truly powerful Gilded Ones to stop all this?"the voice said, mild and conversational. "Hmm. I expect them to arrive in time. They’re likely still grasping what’s happening, with all the attacks landing across THE Braneworld from so many directions at once. It’s a lot to take in. But they’ll get here. Don’t be so pressed about it."
HUUM!
Dietrich’s face went livid, because he knew that voice. It was the voice of the existence he detested above all others.
He turned.
THE Infiltrator. THE Defiler of his sister.This motherfucker!

He stood there adorned in a blue robe that shone with an Infinity Dietrich could not fathom, an Infinity so dense that looking at the being made Dietrich’s eyes burn as though he had turned them toward a sun. He kept looking anyway, defiant, refusing to look away from the thing he hated, and he kept looking even when he felt his eyes begin to bleed, the burning intensifying until crimson-gold ran down his cheeks, and still he glared, because to look away was to concede, and Dietrich would die before he conceded to THE Defiler. The being was vile to his sight. Cruel. Filled with hatred, a villain wearing a man’s shape, and Dietrich would name him for exactly what he was until his last breath!
In the next moment, a hand clamped onto his neck.
CRACK!

The Defiler lifted him bodily into the air, fingers closing around his throat, the bones of his neck grinding toward shattering under a grip that held terrifying power in it, and Dietrich felt himself raised up like an animal hauled to slaughter!

"You know, I’m normally very laid back," THE Defiler said, holding him aloft. "Genuinely. I don’t care for cruelty. I don’t care for unnecessary destruction. It bores me, mostly, the beings who reach for it first. I’d much rather grow things than break them."

His blue eyes were cold. "But every so often, some lifeforms live with such vileness, such detestable weavings woven all the way through their existences, that I have to bear witness to a little destruction whether I want to or not. Consider this one of those times."
Dietrich refuted it in his soul even as his neck creaked!

How dare this thing speak of vileness! How dare THE Defiler call anyone cruel! How much crueler could a being possibly be than to strip away everything that made a lifeform what it was? The Pride. The Infinity. The very self! There was no torture in all the methods of the Gilded Ones that matched it.
"You are crueler than all of us, Defiler! You are the cruelest thing in existence!"
HUUM!
He spat the thought out loud, the words breaking around the grip on his throat, and THE Defiler turned to him with a dangerous smile and waved his free hand.
And Dietrich saw them appear.

Billions of lifeforms, carrying a silver Acedia brilliance, materializing around the dead Citadel. Billions. And more pressing in from the periphery, an ocean of them with no visible end. They looked like lost things, hollow things, no weavings of intelligence in their eyes, no will, nothing behind the silver glow but emptiness. Existences that had been emptied of everything except motion!

"These are Existential Acedia Dredges,"THE Defiler said pleasantly. "Bounded Lifeforms, once. The ones who had the Acedia Ordnances dropped on them, on the whole of the Observable Existence down below. Quintillions, mindless now, their selves burned out of them by your Houses careful methodology."He surveyed the gathering sea.
